609.claim: Increased flux of microbial products provokes immune responses.
609.raw:
VERDICT: SUPPORTED
EXPLANATION: Abstract [21439293] discusses how the immune system evaluates the level of microbial threat, proposing five immune checkpoints that determine the gravity of microbial encounters. This implies that there is a complex evaluation process involving microbial viability, which can provoke immune responses. Abstract [4394525] further supports this by showing that bacteria can directly activate sensory neurons, inducing pain and inflammation, suggesting that microbial products can indeed provoke immune responses. Abstract [20148808] provides additional context by linking the microbiome to allergic lung inflammation, indicating that microbial products can influence immune responses beyond just direct activation. Abstract [37969403] complements this by discussing cytokine production and lymphoproliferative responses following oral immunization with attenuated Salmonella typhi strains, reinforcing the idea that microbial products can provoke immune responses.
